marcos-sem-mc-01-servo-autoridade-01.question: In Mark 1:15, Jesus says the kingdom of God is near and calls for repentance and faith in the gospel.
marcos-sem-mc-01-servo-autoridade-01.feedbackCorrect: Jesus announces the kingdom is near and calls for repentance and faith.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread Mark 1:15 and see Jesus' announcement and call.

marcos-sem-mc-01-servo-autoridade-02.question: In Mark 1:11, tap how the voice from heaven calls Jesus.
marcos-sem-mc-01-servo-autoridade-02.feedbackCorrect: The voice calls Jesus the beloved Son, in whom God delights.

feedbackWrong.a: The voice from heaven is who speaks, not how Jesus is called.
feedbackWrong.c: That says God's delight, not the name given to Jesus.

marcos-sem-mc-01-servo-autoridade-02.hint: Look for the name the voice gives Jesus.

marcos-sem-mc-01-servo-autoridade-03.question: According to Mark 1:16, what were Simon and Andrew doing by the sea?
marcos-sem-mc-01-servo-autoridade-03.feedbackCorrect: They were casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.

feedbackWrong.b: The text shows them fishing, not selling.
feedbackWrong.c: Their work is fishing, not farming.
feedbackWrong.d: They are by the sea, casting the net.

marcos-sem-mc-01-servo-autoridade-03.hint: See their work in the verse.

options.a: Casting a net into the sea
options.b: Selling fish at the market

marcos-sem-mc-01-servo-autoridade-04.question: Put Mark 1:15 in the order of the text.
marcos-sem-mc-01-servo-autoridade-04.feedbackCorrect: Time fulfilled, kingdom near, and the call to repent and believe.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the time fulfilled; the call closes the verse.

marcos-sem-mc-01-servo-autoridade-04.hint: The verse begins with the time.

marcos-sem-mc-01-servo-autoridade-05.question: In Mark 1:15, how does Jesus say the kingdom of God is?
marcos-sem-mc-01-servo-autoridade-05.feedbackCorrect: The kingdom is near: God has drawn close to people.

feedbackWrong.b: Jesus says the opposite: the kingdom has come near.
feedbackWrong.c: Jesus announces the kingdom openly, not in secret.

marcos-sem-mc-01-servo-autoridade-05.hint: Read the middle of the verse.

marcos-sem-mc-01-servo-autoridade-06.question: What does Mark 1:14 communicate that ties into this context?
marcos-sem-mc-01-servo-autoridade-06.feedbackCorrect: After John's arrest, Jesus goes to Galilee to preach.

feedbackWrong.b: It is precisely to Galilee that Jesus takes the gospel.
feedbackWrong.c: John was arrested; now Jesus is the one preaching.

marcos-sem-mc-01-servo-autoridade-06.hint: See who preaches and where, in that verse.

options.a: Jesus begins his public announcement
options.b: Galilee has no need of the gospel

marcos-cam-mc-01-servo-autoridade-01.question: In Mark 1:14–15, Jesus announces the kingdom but postpones any response from people until later.
marcos-cam-mc-01-servo-autoridade-01.feedbackCorrect: The announcement already comes with an immediate call: repentance and faith.

feedbackWrong.true: The call comes with the announcement: repent and believe.

marcos-cam-mc-01-servo-autoridade-01.hint: See what Jesus asks for in the same announcement.

marcos-cam-mc-01-servo-autoridade-02.question: In Mark 1:14, tap the word that marks what happens right after John's arrest.
marcos-cam-mc-01-servo-autoridade-02.feedbackCorrect: The word opens the verse and links John's arrest to Jesus' step.

feedbackWrong.a: That is the earlier fact, not the linking word.
feedbackWrong.b: That is the place Jesus goes to.

marcos-cam-mc-01-servo-autoridade-02.hint: Look for the first word of the verse.

marcos-cam-mc-01-servo-autoridade-03.question: What does the nearness of the kingdom ask of people in Mark 1:15?
marcos-cam-mc-01-servo-autoridade-03.feedbackCorrect: The near kingdom asks for a change of direction and faith in the good news.

feedbackWrong.a: Trust is in God's good news, not in merit.
feedbackWrong.b: The kingdom is near, not far from God.
feedbackWrong.d: Jesus asks for a response, not passive waiting.

marcos-cam-mc-01-servo-autoridade-03.hint: Put together the two calls at the end of the verse.

options.a: Trust only in your own merits
options.b: Seek a kingdom far from God
options.c: Change direction and trust the news
options.d: Wait for the kingdom without changing anything

marcos-cam-mc-01-servo-autoridade-04.question: How does the scene unfold in Mark 1:14–15?
marcos-cam-mc-01-servo-autoridade-04.feedbackCorrect: John's arrest, going to Galilee, and the announcement of the kingdom.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with John's arrest; the announcement comes after.

options.a: John is arrested
options.b: Jesus goes to Galilee to preach
options.c: He announces the kingdom is near

marcos-cam-mc-01-servo-autoridade-05.question: In Mark 1:17, what does Jesus say he will make Simon and Andrew?
marcos-cam-mc-01-servo-autoridade-05.feedbackCorrect: From fishers of fish, they will gather people for God.

feedbackWrong.a: Jesus uses the image of their work: the sea and the nets.
feedbackWrong.c: The call uses their trade, not a teaching title.

marcos-cam-mc-01-servo-autoridade-05.hint: Jesus starts from the trade they already have.

marcos-cam-mc-01-servo-autoridade-06.question: What connects Mark 1:15 to Matthew 4:17?
marcos-cam-mc-01-servo-autoridade-06.feedbackCorrect: In both texts, the near kingdom calls for repentance.

feedbackWrong.a: In both, the announcement comes with a call to change.
feedbackWrong.c: The kingdom draws near to people; it does not pull away.

marcos-cam-mc-01-servo-autoridade-06.hint: Compare the call that accompanies the announcement.

options.a: Preaching without a call to change
options.b: The kingdom calls for repentance

marcos-pro-mc-01-servo-autoridade-01.question: In Mark 1:17–18, following Jesus begins with leaving the nets behind.
marcos-pro-mc-01-servo-autoridade-01.feedbackCorrect: They leave the nets right away and follow Jesus.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread Mark 1:18: they leave the nets, and they follow him.

marcos-pro-mc-01-servo-autoridade-02.question: In Mark 1:18, tap what Simon and Andrew leave to follow Jesus.
marcos-pro-mc-01-servo-autoridade-02.feedbackCorrect: They leave the tool of their livelihood to follow him.

feedbackWrong.a: That is what they do after leaving.
feedbackWrong.b: That says how fast, not what was left.

marcos-pro-mc-01-servo-autoridade-02.hint: Look for the object tied to their work.

marcos-pro-mc-01-servo-autoridade-03.question: What reading does Mark 1:11–12 support about Jesus at the start of the Gospel?
marcos-pro-mc-01-servo-autoridade-03.feedbackCorrect: Before acting, Jesus is declared the beloved Son by heaven.

feedbackWrong.b: The voice confirms who he is; it is not a test to pass.
feedbackWrong.c: The voice speaks of a beloved Son, not a political office.
feedbackWrong.d: The Spirit drives him into the wilderness; he does not abandon him.

marcos-pro-mc-01-servo-autoridade-03.hint: Put together the voice from heaven and the Spirit's action.

options.a: Jesus is the beloved Son confirmed by heaven
options.b: Jesus must prove he is the Son
options.c: The voice declares a political king
options.d: The Spirit abandons Jesus in the wilderness

marcos-pro-mc-01-servo-autoridade-04.question: Which sequence reveals Jesus' path at the start of Mark?
marcos-pro-mc-01-servo-autoridade-04.feedbackCorrect: Son confirmed, kingdom announced, and disciples who follow.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the voice from heaven, before the announcement in Galilee.

marcos-pro-mc-01-servo-autoridade-04.hint: Follow the order of Mark chapter one.

options.a: The voice declares Jesus the beloved Son
options.b: Jesus announces the kingdom in Galilee
options.c: Fishermen leave their nets and follow him

marcos-pro-mc-01-servo-autoridade-05.question: In Mark 1:15, what does Jesus say about the time?
marcos-pro-mc-01-servo-autoridade-05.feedbackCorrect: The time is fulfilled: the waiting is over and the kingdom has come.

feedbackWrong.b: Time was not wasted; it was fulfilled in Jesus.
feedbackWrong.c: Jesus does not delay: he announces that the time has come.

marcos-pro-mc-01-servo-autoridade-05.hint: It is the first statement of the announcement.

marcos-pro-mc-01-servo-autoridade-06.question: What connects Mark 1:17 to Mark 10:45?
marcos-pro-mc-01-servo-autoridade-06.feedbackCorrect: Those who follow Jesus enter the path of the Servant who serves.

feedbackWrong.a: The first disciples leave their nets to follow him.
feedbackWrong.b: The Servant came to serve, not to seek the first place.

marcos-pro-mc-01-servo-autoridade-06.hint: See what the Son of Man came for, in the second text.

options.a: Follow without leaving anything
options.b: Seek the first place

marcos-sem-mc-02-caminho-cruz-01.question: In Mark 8:31, Jesus teaches that the Son of Man would be acclaimed by the leaders and spared from death.
marcos-sem-mc-02-caminho-cruz-01.feedbackCorrect: Jesus announces rejection, death, and resurrection on the third day.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread Mark 8:31: he would be rejected and killed.

marcos-sem-mc-02-caminho-cruz-01.hint: See what the leaders would do to him.

marcos-sem-mc-02-caminho-cruz-02.question: In Mark 8:31, tap after how long the Son of Man would rise.
marcos-sem-mc-02-caminho-cruz-02.feedbackCorrect: Jesus announces he would rise after three days.

feedbackWrong.a: They are among those who would reject him.
feedbackWrong.b: That is what he would suffer, not the time of the resurrection.

marcos-sem-mc-02-caminho-cruz-02.hint: Look for the time frame at the end of the verse.

marcos-sem-mc-02-caminho-cruz-03.question: According to Mark 8:34, whom does Jesus call together to hear the call?
marcos-sem-mc-02-caminho-cruz-03.feedbackCorrect: The call is open: the crowd and the disciples hear it together.

feedbackWrong.a: The summons includes the crowd, not just family.
feedbackWrong.c: The priests are among those who reject Jesus.
feedbackWrong.d: Peter was rebuked earlier; the call is for everyone there.

marcos-sem-mc-02-caminho-cruz-03.hint: See whom Jesus gathers before speaking.

options.a: Only his family
options.b: The crowd and his disciples

marcos-sem-mc-02-caminho-cruz-04.question: Put Mark 8:31 in the order of the text.
marcos-sem-mc-02-caminho-cruz-04.feedbackCorrect: Teaching, suffering and death, with resurrection on the third day.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with Jesus' teaching; the resurrection closes it.

marcos-sem-mc-02-caminho-cruz-04.hint: The verse begins with Jesus teaching.

marcos-sem-mc-02-caminho-cruz-05.question: In Mark 8:34, what must those who follow Jesus take up?
marcos-sem-mc-02-caminho-cruz-05.feedbackCorrect: Following Jesus includes taking up your own cross, as he teaches.

feedbackWrong.a: The nets were left behind in the fishermen's call.
feedbackWrong.b: The call is to take up something tied to surrender, not to home.

marcos-sem-mc-02-caminho-cruz-05.hint: It is Jesus' second request in the verse.

marcos-sem-mc-02-caminho-cruz-06.question: What does Mark 8:34 communicate that ties into this context?
marcos-sem-mc-02-caminho-cruz-06.feedbackCorrect: The first step of the call is to deny yourself.

feedbackWrong.a: Jesus asks the opposite of seeking your own glory.
feedbackWrong.c: The path includes loss for Jesus' sake.

marcos-sem-mc-02-caminho-cruz-06.hint: See the first request in the verse.

options.a: Seek your own glory
options.b: Deny yourself

marcos-cam-mc-02-caminho-cruz-01.question: In Mark 8:34–35, Jesus links saving life to losing it for his sake and the gospel's.
marcos-cam-mc-02-caminho-cruz-01.feedbackCorrect: Losing your life for Jesus and the gospel is saving it.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread Mark 8:35: whoever loses it for Jesus will save it.

marcos-cam-mc-02-caminho-cruz-01.hint: Compare saving and losing in verse 35.

marcos-cam-mc-02-caminho-cruz-02.question: In Mark 8:33, tap the word that contrasts the things of God with those of men.
marcos-cam-mc-02-caminho-cruz-02.feedbackCorrect: The word separates two ways of thinking: God's and the human one.

feedbackWrong.a: That limits Peter's thinking; it does not contrast the parts.
feedbackWrong.c: That begins the explanation; it does not mark the contrast.

marcos-cam-mc-02-caminho-cruz-02.hint: Look for a short word between the two ideas.

marcos-cam-mc-02-caminho-cruz-03.question: Why does Jesus rebuke Peter in Mark 8:32–33?
marcos-cam-mc-02-caminho-cruz-03.feedbackCorrect: Peter rebukes the cross because he thinks only in a human way.

feedbackWrong.b: The text says nothing about a trip or a deadline.
feedbackWrong.c: The conversation is private; the problem is the way of thinking.
feedbackWrong.d: Peter rebukes Jesus' suffering; he is not defending others.

marcos-cam-mc-02-caminho-cruz-03.hint: See the reason Jesus himself states.

options.a: Peter judges by human desire, not by God's way
options.b: Peter wants to postpone the trip to Jerusalem
options.c: Peter speaks too loudly before the crowd
options.d: Peter defends the other disciples from suffering

marcos-cam-mc-02-caminho-cruz-04.question: How do the events of Mark 8:32–33 link together?
marcos-cam-mc-02-caminho-cruz-04.feedbackCorrect: Peter calls him aside, rebukes him, and Jesus then rebukes Peter.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with Peter taking Jesus aside.

options.a: Peter takes Jesus aside
options.b: Peter begins to rebuke him

marcos-cam-mc-02-caminho-cruz-05.question: In Mark 8:35, what happens to whoever wants to save their life?
marcos-cam-mc-02-caminho-cruz-05.feedbackCorrect: Clinging to your own life ends up losing it.

feedbackWrong.a: The exchange of the soul appears in the following verses.
feedbackWrong.c: Jesus says the opposite of holding on to life this way.

marcos-cam-mc-02-caminho-cruz-05.hint: Read the first half of the verse.

marcos-cam-mc-02-caminho-cruz-06.question: What connects Mark 8:34 to Mark 10:45?
marcos-cam-mc-02-caminho-cruz-06.feedbackCorrect: Following Jesus is walking behind the Son who came to serve.

feedbackWrong.a: The Son came to serve, not to be served.
feedbackWrong.b: Jesus' way is one of serving others.

marcos-cam-mc-02-caminho-cruz-06.hint: See what the Son of Man came for.

options.a: The greatest seeks to be served
options.b: Follow without serving anyone

marcos-pro-mc-02-caminho-cruz-01.question: In Mark 8:38, Jesus says being ashamed of him has no future consequence.
marcos-pro-mc-02-caminho-cruz-01.feedbackCorrect: There is a consequence: the Son of Man will be ashamed of whoever denied him.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread the end: the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him.

marcos-pro-mc-02-caminho-cruz-01.hint: See what happens when the Son comes.

marcos-pro-mc-02-caminho-cruz-02.question: In Mark 8:36, tap what is worth nothing to gain if the soul is lost.
marcos-pro-mc-02-caminho-cruz-02.feedbackCorrect: Not even the whole world makes up for losing your own soul.

feedbackWrong.a: The soul is what is lost, not what is gained.
feedbackWrong.c: That is who the question is addressed to.

marcos-pro-mc-02-caminho-cruz-02.hint: Look for the gain Jesus compares to the soul.

marcos-pro-mc-02-caminho-cruz-03.question: What reading does Mark 8:35–36 support about gaining and losing?
marcos-pro-mc-02-caminho-cruz-03.feedbackCorrect: The greatest gain becomes total loss if the soul is lost.

feedbackWrong.a: Nothing makes up for the soul, not even the whole world.
feedbackWrong.c: Whoever clings to life loses it, says Jesus.
feedbackWrong.d: The announced path goes through the cross; it does not avoid it.

marcos-pro-mc-02-caminho-cruz-03.hint: Put together the warning of verse 35 and the question of 36.

options.a: The soul is worth less than success
options.b: Gaining everything and losing your soul is total loss
options.c: Protecting your life is the highest good
options.d: Jesus promises glory without a cross

marcos-pro-mc-02-caminho-cruz-04.question: Which sequence reveals the meaning of Mark 8:31–38?
marcos-pro-mc-02-caminho-cruz-04.feedbackCorrect: Announcement of the cross, call to follow him, and future glory.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the announcement of Jesus' suffering.

marcos-pro-mc-02-caminho-cruz-04.hint: Follow from Jesus' announcement to his future coming.

options.a: Jesus announces he will suffer and rise
options.b: Jesus calls people to take up the cross
options.c: The Son will come in the Father's glory

marcos-pro-mc-02-caminho-cruz-05.question: In Mark 8:34, what does Jesus ask first of anyone who wants to follow him?
marcos-pro-mc-02-caminho-cruz-05.feedbackCorrect: Before the cross, the disciple denies himself.

feedbackWrong.a: Protecting yourself is the path that loses life (8:35).
feedbackWrong.b: The request is the opposite of exalting yourself.

marcos-pro-mc-02-caminho-cruz-05.hint: It is the first request in Jesus' list.

marcos-pro-mc-02-caminho-cruz-06.question: What connects Mark 8:35 to John 12:24?
marcos-pro-mc-02-caminho-cruz-06.feedbackCorrect: Like the grain that dies, losing for Jesus brings life.

feedbackWrong.b: The grain kept back stays alone; the one that dies bears fruit.
feedbackWrong.c: In both texts, surrender opens the way to life.

marcos-pro-mc-02-caminho-cruz-06.hint: See what happens to the grain in the second text.

options.a: Losing life bears fruit
options.b: Keeping life bears fruit

marcos-sem-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-01.question: In Mark 16:4, the women saw that the stone had already been rolled away.
marcos-sem-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-01.feedbackCorrect: Looking up, they see the stone already out of place.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread Mark 16:4: the stone had already been rolled away.

marcos-sem-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-01.hint: See what they find when they look.

marcos-sem-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-02.question: In Mark 16:4, tap what the tomb's stone was like.
marcos-sem-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-02.feedbackCorrect: The stone was very large, and even so it had already been rolled away.

feedbackWrong.a: That is its state, not its size.
feedbackWrong.b: That is what the women do, not the stone.

marcos-sem-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-02.hint: Look for the size at the end of the verse.

marcos-sem-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-03.question: According to Mark 16:5, what did the women see on entering the tomb?
marcos-sem-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-03.feedbackCorrect: They see a young man in white, seated on the right.

feedbackWrong.a: The text does not mention guards in this scene.
feedbackWrong.c: Inside is a young man, not the disciples.
feedbackWrong.d: The body is not there, as the young man announces.

marcos-sem-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-03.hint: Read who is inside the tomb.

options.a: Guards sleeping at the entrance
options.b: A young man seated, dressed in white

marcos-sem-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-04.question: Put Mark 16:6 in the order of the text.
marcos-sem-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-04.feedbackCorrect: Calm, whom they seek, and the announcement: he has risen.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the young man's words of calm.

marcos-sem-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-04.hint: The young man begins by calming the women.

marcos-sem-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-05.question: In Mark 16:6, what does the young man say Jesus did?
marcos-sem-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-05.feedbackCorrect: The announcement is direct: he has risen and is not here.

feedbackWrong.a: The place is empty because he lives, not because he sleeps.
feedbackWrong.c: He did not flee: the young man announces something greater.

marcos-sem-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-05.hint: It is the central news of the verse.

marcos-sem-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-06.question: What does Mark 16:6 communicate that ties into this context?
marcos-sem-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-06.feedbackCorrect: The crucified one has risen: death did not hold him.

feedbackWrong.a: The cross was real; the victory comes after it.
feedbackWrong.b: The young man says he is no longer there.

marcos-sem-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-06.hint: See the announcement about where Jesus is.

options.a: The cross was only an illusion
options.b: Jesus is still in the tomb

marcos-cam-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-01.question: In Mark 16:7, the young man tells the women to keep silent and tell no one.
marcos-cam-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-01.feedbackCorrect: The order is to go and tell the disciples and Peter.

feedbackWrong.true: The order is the opposite: go and tell the disciples.

marcos-cam-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-01.hint: Read the order the young man gives.

marcos-cam-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-02.question: In Mark 16:6, tap the word that turns the women's fear into an announcement.
marcos-cam-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-02.feedbackCorrect: The word opens the speech that calms and announces.

feedbackWrong.b: That shows whom he is speaking to, not the turn.
feedbackWrong.c: That points to the empty place, not the turn.

marcos-cam-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-02.hint: Look for the first word of the verse.

marcos-cam-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-03.question: How does Mark 16:4 answer the worry of Mark 16:3?
marcos-cam-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-03.feedbackCorrect: The feared obstacle was already resolved when they looked.

feedbackWrong.b: They do not remove it: when they looked, the stone was already out of the way.
feedbackWrong.c: They see the stone already removed, not the moment of removal.
feedbackWrong.d: The text does not mention guards in this scene.

marcos-cam-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-03.hint: Compare the question of verse 3 with verse 4.

options.a: The feared stone no longer seals the tomb
options.b: The women roll the stone away together
options.c: The stone vanishes before their eyes
options.d: Guards open the tomb at their request

marcos-cam-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-04.question: How does the scene unfold in Mark 16:5–6?
marcos-cam-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-04.feedbackCorrect: Entering, meeting the young man, and the announcement they hear.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with their entering the tomb.

marcos-cam-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-04.hint: The announcement comes after they enter.

options.a: The women enter the tomb
options.b: They see a young man in white
options.c: They hear that Jesus has risen

marcos-cam-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-05.question: In Mark 16:7, where does the young man say Jesus is going ahead of them?
marcos-cam-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-05.feedbackCorrect: Jesus is going ahead to Galilee, as he had said.

feedbackWrong.a: The appointed meeting is in Galilee, not Jerusalem.
feedbackWrong.b: The destination the young man names is another, to the north.

marcos-cam-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-05.hint: It is the place of the promised meeting.

marcos-cam-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-06.question: What connects Mark 16:6 to Mark 8:31?
marcos-cam-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-06.feedbackCorrect: Jesus had already announced he would die and rise (8:31).

feedbackWrong.a: In 8:31 he speaks openly of death and resurrection.
feedbackWrong.b: He himself announced this earlier, in Mark 8:31.

marcos-cam-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-06.hint: See what Jesus taught in Mark 8:31.

options.a: Jesus avoided talking about death
options.b: The resurrection was total improvisation

marcos-pro-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-01.question: In Mark 16:6, the young man links the Jesus they seek to the cross and announces that he has risen.
marcos-pro-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-01.feedbackCorrect: The risen one is the same Jesus who was crucified.

feedbackWrong.false: The young man names the crucified one and announces: he has risen.

marcos-pro-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-01.hint: See how the young man identifies Jesus.

marcos-pro-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-02.question: In Mark 16:5, tap how the young man in the tomb was dressed.
marcos-pro-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-02.feedbackCorrect: The young man is dressed in white, seated on the right.

feedbackWrong.a: That says his position, not his clothing.
feedbackWrong.b: That says the place, not how he was dressed.

marcos-pro-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-02.hint: Look for the clothing, at the end of the description.

marcos-pro-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-03.question: What reading does Mark 16:6–7 support about the resurrection?
marcos-pro-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-03.feedbackCorrect: The crucified one lives and goes ahead of the disciples.

feedbackWrong.a: The young man names Peter in the message, including him.
feedbackWrong.c: The announcement is of resurrection, not of a hiding place.
feedbackWrong.d: There is an empty place and an appointed meeting, not just a feeling.

marcos-pro-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-03.hint: Put together the announcement of verse 6 and the message of 7.

options.a: Peter is left out of the young man's announcement
options.b: The crucified one has risen and goes ahead of them
options.c: Jesus' body was hidden by the women
options.d: The resurrection is only a feeling of the disciples

marcos-pro-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-04.question: Which sequence reveals the meaning of Mark 16:6–7?
marcos-pro-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-04.feedbackCorrect: Seeking the crucified one, announcing the resurrection, and the meeting.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with whom they are seeking in the tomb.

marcos-pro-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-04.hint: Follow from the search to the appointed meeting.

options.a: The women seek the crucified Jesus
options.b: The young man announces he has risen

marcos-pro-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-05.question: In Mark 16:3, what did the women fear they could not remove?
marcos-pro-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-05.feedbackCorrect: Their worry was the huge stone at the entrance.

feedbackWrong.b: The cross was left behind; the obstacle is at the tomb's entrance.
feedbackWrong.c: The obstacle named on the way is another, a very heavy one.

marcos-pro-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-05.hint: Recall their worry on the way.

marcos-pro-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-06.question: What connects Mark 16:7 to Mark 14:28?
marcos-pro-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-06.feedbackCorrect: Jesus had already promised to go ahead of them to Galilee.

feedbackWrong.a: He had said this before, in Mark 14:28.
feedbackWrong.c: Peter is named in the message, not left out.

marcos-pro-mc-03-cruz-ressurreicao-06.hint: Compare the destination with Jesus' earlier promise.

options.a: Galilee was a new plan
options.b: Jesus fulfills what he promised

marcos-sem-mc-boss-revisao-01.question: In Mark 1:18, Simon and Andrew asked for time to sell their nets before following Jesus.
marcos-sem-mc-boss-revisao-01.feedbackCorrect: They leave the nets immediately and follow him.

feedbackWrong.true: There is no delay: they leave the nets right away.

marcos-sem-mc-boss-revisao-02.question: In Mark 1:17, tap what Jesus will make Simon and Andrew.
marcos-sem-mc-boss-revisao-02.feedbackCorrect: From fishers of fish, they will gather people for God.

feedbackWrong.a: That is the call to come, not the new task.
feedbackWrong.b: That introduces the speech; it does not name the task.

marcos-sem-mc-boss-revisao-02.hint: Look for the new task at the end of the speech.

marcos-sem-mc-boss-revisao-03.question: According to Mark 8:31, what does Jesus teach about the Son of Man?
marcos-sem-mc-boss-revisao-03.feedbackCorrect: Jesus announces suffering, death, and resurrection.

feedbackWrong.a: He would be rejected by the leaders, says the text.
feedbackWrong.b: He announces rejection and death, not acclaim.
feedbackWrong.c: The announced path is the cross, not an army.

options.a: He will avoid any rejection by the leaders
options.b: He will be acclaimed and spared from death
options.c: He will gather an army in Jerusalem
options.d: He will suffer, die, and rise

marcos-sem-mc-boss-revisao-04.question: Put Mark 16:6 in the order of the text.
marcos-sem-mc-boss-revisao-04.feedbackCorrect: Calm, whom they seek, and the announcement: he has risen.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the young man's words of calm.

marcos-sem-mc-boss-revisao-04.hint: The young man begins by calming the women.

marcos-sem-mc-boss-revisao-05.question: In Mark 1:15, in what does Jesus ask people to believe?
marcos-sem-mc-boss-revisao-05.feedbackCorrect: The faith Jesus asks for is in God's good news.

feedbackWrong.a: The call is to believe the good news, not to live in fear.
feedbackWrong.b: Jesus calls for open faith in the news, not for silence.

marcos-sem-mc-boss-revisao-05.hint: It is the good news Jesus announced.

marcos-sem-mc-boss-revisao-06.question: What does Mark 8:34 communicate that ties into this context?
marcos-sem-mc-boss-revisao-06.feedbackCorrect: The first step of the call is to deny yourself.

feedbackWrong.a: Jesus asks the opposite of seeking your own glory.
feedbackWrong.c: The path includes loss for Jesus' sake.

marcos-sem-mc-boss-revisao-06.hint: See the first request in the verse.

options.a: Seek your own glory
options.b: Deny yourself

marcos-sem-mc-boss-revisao-07.question: In Mark 16:4, tap what had already been removed when the women looked.
marcos-sem-mc-boss-revisao-07.feedbackCorrect: The enormous obstacle was already out of place.

feedbackWrong.a: That is its state, not the object removed.
feedbackWrong.c: That is its size, not the object.

marcos-sem-mc-boss-revisao-07.hint: Look for the object before its state.

marcos-sem-mc-boss-revisao-08.question: Put Mark 8:34 in the order of the text.
marcos-sem-mc-boss-revisao-08.feedbackCorrect: Deny yourself, take up the cross, and follow Jesus, in that order.
marcos-sem-mc-boss-revisao-08.hint: The first request is about yourself.

marcos-cam-mc-boss-revisao-01.question: In Mark 8:35, Jesus teaches that protecting your own life at any cost is the way to save it.
marcos-cam-mc-boss-revisao-01.feedbackCorrect: Clinging to your own life is losing it, says Jesus.

feedbackWrong.true: Jesus says the opposite: whoever wants to save it that way loses it.

marcos-cam-mc-boss-revisao-01.hint: Compare saving and losing in the verse.

marcos-cam-mc-boss-revisao-02.question: In Mark 8:33, tap the word that contrasts the things of God with those of men.
marcos-cam-mc-boss-revisao-02.feedbackCorrect: The word separates God's thinking from human thinking.

feedbackWrong.a: That begins the explanation; it does not mark the contrast.
feedbackWrong.c: That limits Peter's thinking; it does not contrast.

marcos-cam-mc-boss-revisao-02.hint: Look for a short word between the ideas.

marcos-cam-mc-boss-revisao-03.question: What does the nearness of the kingdom ask for, in Mark 1:15?
marcos-cam-mc-boss-revisao-03.feedbackCorrect: The near kingdom asks for a change of direction and faith.

feedbackWrong.a: The kingdom is near, not distant.
feedbackWrong.b: Jesus asks for a response, not passive waiting.
feedbackWrong.d: Trust is in God's good news.

marcos-cam-mc-boss-revisao-03.hint: Put together the two calls of the announcement.

options.a: Seek a distant kingdom
options.b: Wait without changing direction

marcos-cam-mc-boss-revisao-04.question: How does the scene unfold in Mark 1:14–15?
marcos-cam-mc-boss-revisao-04.feedbackCorrect: John's arrest, going to Galilee, and announcing the kingdom.

options.a: John is arrested
options.b: Jesus goes to Galilee to preach
options.c: He announces the kingdom is near

marcos-cam-mc-boss-revisao-05.question: In Mark 8:35, whoever loses their life for Jesus will do what with it?
marcos-cam-mc-boss-revisao-05.feedbackCorrect: Losing it for Jesus and the gospel is saving your life.

feedbackWrong.a: Losing is the path; the result stated is the other verb.
feedbackWrong.b: Holding back is the path Jesus says loses life.

marcos-cam-mc-boss-revisao-05.hint: Read the result at the end of the verse.

marcos-cam-mc-boss-revisao-06.question: What connects Mark 8:34 to Mark 10:45?
marcos-cam-mc-boss-revisao-06.feedbackCorrect: Following Jesus is walking behind the Son who came to serve.

feedbackWrong.a: The Son came to serve, not to be served.
feedbackWrong.c: Jesus' way is one of serving others.

marcos-cam-mc-boss-revisao-06.hint: See what the Son came for.

options.a: The greatest seeks to be served
options.b: The Son came to serve

marcos-cam-mc-boss-revisao-07.question: In Mark 1:14, tap the word that marks the step after John's arrest.
marcos-cam-mc-boss-revisao-07.feedbackCorrect: The word opens the verse and marks the sequence.

feedbackWrong.b: That is the earlier fact, not the link.
feedbackWrong.c: That is the place Jesus goes to.

marcos-cam-mc-boss-revisao-07.hint: Look for the first word of the verse.

marcos-cam-mc-boss-revisao-08.question: How do the events of Mark 16:3–4 link together?
marcos-cam-mc-boss-revisao-08.feedbackCorrect: A worried question, a look, and the stone already removed.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the women's question on the way.

marcos-cam-mc-boss-revisao-08.hint: The worry comes before the look.

options.a: The women ask about the stone
options.b: They look at the tomb
options.c: They see the stone already removed

marcos-pro-mc-boss-revisao-01.question: In Mark 16:6, the empty tomb goes with the announcement that the crucified Jesus has risen.
marcos-pro-mc-boss-revisao-01.feedbackCorrect: The risen one is the crucified one, and the place is empty.

feedbackWrong.false: The young man announces: he has risen, he is not here.

marcos-pro-mc-boss-revisao-01.hint: Put the announcement together with the empty place.

marcos-pro-mc-boss-revisao-02.question: In Mark 16:6, tap how the young man identifies the Jesus they seek.
marcos-pro-mc-boss-revisao-02.feedbackCorrect: The risen one is identified as the crucified one.

feedbackWrong.b: That is his origin, not what happened to him.
feedbackWrong.c: That describes the women, not Jesus.

marcos-pro-mc-boss-revisao-02.hint: Look for what happened to Jesus before.

marcos-pro-mc-boss-revisao-03.question: What reading does Mark 16:7 support about Peter?
marcos-pro-mc-boss-revisao-03.feedbackCorrect: Peter is named in the message: he is called too.

feedbackWrong.a: In Galilee they will see him, as he said.
feedbackWrong.b: The order is to go and tell, not to be silent.
feedbackWrong.d: The young man names him precisely to include him.

marcos-pro-mc-boss-revisao-03.hint: See whom the young man names in the message.

options.a: Galilee cancels the promised meeting
options.b: The women must stay silent forever
options.c: Peter also receives the young man's message
options.d: Peter is excluded for having failed

marcos-pro-mc-boss-revisao-04.question: Which sequence reveals Jesus' path in Mark?
marcos-pro-mc-boss-revisao-04.feedbackCorrect: Kingdom announced, path of the cross, and resurrection.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the announcement of the kingdom in Galilee.

marcos-pro-mc-boss-revisao-04.hint: Follow from the start of Mark to the empty tomb.

options.a: Jesus announces the kingdom is near
options.b: Jesus calls people to take up the cross
options.c: Jesus rises and goes ahead of them

marcos-pro-mc-boss-revisao-05.question: In Mark 16:7, to whom does the young man tell them to give the message, besides Peter?
marcos-pro-mc-boss-revisao-05.feedbackCorrect: The message is for the disciples, with Peter named.

feedbackWrong.b: The priests do not receive this message in the text.
feedbackWrong.c: The text does not tell them to notify the tomb guards.

marcos-pro-mc-boss-revisao-05.hint: Read the beginning of the young man's order.

marcos-pro-mc-boss-revisao-06.question: What connects Mark 8:35 to John 12:24?
marcos-pro-mc-boss-revisao-06.feedbackCorrect: Like the grain that dies, losing for Jesus brings life.

feedbackWrong.b: In both texts, surrender opens the way to life.
feedbackWrong.c: The grain kept back stays alone; the one that dies bears fruit.

marcos-pro-mc-boss-revisao-06.hint: See what happens to the grain.

options.a: Losing life bears fruit
options.b: Death ends the path

marcos-pro-mc-boss-revisao-07.question: In Mark 8:36, tap what is worth nothing to gain if the soul is lost.
marcos-pro-mc-boss-revisao-07.feedbackCorrect: Not even the whole world makes up for losing your soul.

feedbackWrong.a: The soul is what is lost, not what is gained.
feedbackWrong.c: That is who the question is addressed to.

marcos-pro-mc-boss-revisao-07.hint: Look for the gain compared to the soul.

marcos-pro-mc-boss-revisao-08.question: Which sequence reveals the conflict of Mark 8:32–34?
marcos-pro-mc-boss-revisao-08.feedbackCorrect: Peter's rebuke, Jesus' reproof, and the call.
marcos-pro-mc-boss-revisao-08.hint: The conflict begins with Peter aside.

options.a: Peter rebukes Jesus' path
options.b: Jesus rebukes Peter
options.c: Jesus calls everyone to take up the cross
